articles.summary: Too many product ideas live in spreadsheets, insights get buried, and teams struggle to rally around a shared roadmap.

articles.title: THE ANTITHESIS PRINCIPLE
articles.summary: Every insight about human behavior has two sides: a tactic for influencing others and a bias to resist yourself. Smart people see the tactic, while wise people also overcome the bias.

articles.title: STRIPE AND SIERRA BUILT THEIR OWN CODING AGENT SYSTEMS. YOU PROBABLY DON'T NEED TO
articles.summary: Most companies should buy coding-agent infrastructure and focus their resources on the context and workflows that make it uniquely valuable. Building internally is worthwhile only when the technology is strategically essential, and the organization can support it as a permanent product.

HOW TO RUN CUSTOMER INTERVIEWS FOR A CAPABILITY YOUR USERS HAVE NEVER EXPERIENCED
articles.summary: Customer research for novel AI products should focus on familiar needs rather than hypothetical interest. Study current workarounds, create a realistic experience, and examine the decisions and outcomes the capability could improve.

articles.title: CLAUDE OPUS 5 REVIEW + BROWSER USE IN CODEX + HOW CURSOR AND A RASPBERRY PI MAKES AI FUN (27 MINUTE VIDEO)
articles.summary: Browser and computer-use agents can handle tedious digital work, from exhaustive QA and persona testing to inbox management, shopping, and remote device setup. They perform best when given room to plan, matched to the right model and effort level, and paired with brief human oversight for verification and final decisions.

articles.title: DESIGN DOESN'T HAVE A FINISH LINE
articles.summary: Design should continue throughout development because the hardest decisions often emerge only after building begins. Keeping designers in the delivery loop helps teams catch mistakes early and avoid efficiently shipping the wrong product.

articles.title: SUBSTACK ASKED FOR VOLUME, THEN SHIPPED A SCANNER
articles.summary: Substack incentivized frequent posting, then introduced an AI detector to police the resulting content. This shifts the burden of verification onto users rather than addressing the platform's growth mechanics.
